gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-m-plus-1: M PLUS 1 reads friendly and open, every e and a showing a wide eye in a fineliner-flat line. And Bruno Ace, with its ruler-straight strokes and slow, one-letter-per-beat pace, makes a bold display contrast above it.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-m-plus-1p: Expressive and a bit stubborn, Bruno Ace draws its heading in a plain, unmodulated outline, while M PLUS 1p keeps every curve end open below. Make the heading small and that outline loses its drama.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-m-plus-2: Distinctive is the right word for Bruno Ace, whose ruler-drawn line leaves its counters connected to the outside and gives headings real presence. M PLUS 2 does the quieter job, a sans-serif with a gaping c and one fixed nib width that keeps text approachable.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-m-plus-code-latin: M PLUS Code Latin looks like neon tubing bent into letters, with a wide pitcher mouth in each c. M PLUS Code Latin would get lost if the heading shrank, since Bruno Ace's lingering, ruler-straight beat needs room to show.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-m-plus-rounded-1c: M PLUS Rounded 1c reads soft and approachable, its terminals stopping short of curling back in. And Bruno Ace, with joins as thick as its strokes, adds a stiffer, drawn-by-ruler heading that makes the sans-serif feel gentler still.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-mandali: Mandali reads easily, with a generous entry into the e's eye that keeps each line light. And Bruno Ace brings a marker-like constant-width heading above it, so a slightly larger body size would let the sans hold its own.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-manjari: Sharp, ruled lines and open counters define Bruno Ace at the top. Manjari follows in a plain sans with wide, unclosed terminals and a steady line weight, giving the heading's lingering rhythm somewhere quiet to land.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-meera-inimai: Meera Inimai has a blueprint feel. Its open-ended curves have room to breathe, so a long stretch of text moves smoothly beneath the more expressive, ruler-drawn character of Bruno Ace.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-metrophobic: Bruno Ace's strokes bend like a paperclip, one character per beat, which gives headings a distinctive, lingering stride. Metrophobic does the opposite job as a plain sans, sending a smooth, unobstructed path around each bend of the text.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-mina: Bruno Ace takes the heading with a ruler-drawn, constant-width line and counters that stay open to the outside. Mina follows as a sans with plain, stitched-thread strokes, and a slightly larger size would let its unclosed round letters breathe.
